name: Multi-core current transformer
summary: CT with several independent magnetic cores on one primary, each with its own secondary for metering or protection.
description: A multi-core CT has one primary passing through two or more separate cores, each with its own secondary winding. Typical MV and HV CTs have one metering core and one or more protection cores, so the single-line diagram shows each core as its own ring on the primary with its ratio and class beside it.

Separate cores mean a fault-saturated protection core does not disturb the metering core, and each can have a different accuracy class. The symbol shows how many cores exist but not which relay or meter each feeds, so every core needs its own designation and cross-reference.
readingNotes: Count the cores and read each ratio and class separately.
Follow each secondary to its own relay or meter.
drawingChecklist: State ratio and class per core
distinction: A multi-core CT has separate magnetic cores; a CT with two secondaries on a common core shares one magnetic circuit.
